Real estate tip

How to read a condo status certificate

The condo's financial health in one package. Here are the pages that matter and the red flags to look for.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
Published November 21, 2026
2-minute readResale condosOntario rules

01The basics

10 daysFor the condo to deliver itAfter it receives the request and payment
$100Maximum feeIncluding taxes; rush service can cost extra
ConditionMake your offer subject to itWith time for your lawyer to review

02The pages that matter

Common expenses

Fees and arrears

Current monthly fees, any increase planned, and anything owed on the unit.

Reserve fund

The savings account

The balance and the latest reserve fund study. Is the plan on track?

Special assessments

Extra charges

Any levied or planned, and why.

Legal proceedings

Lawsuits

Any judgments or court actions involving the corporation.

Budget and financials

Where money goes

The current budget and audited statements.

Rules and insurance

Your daily life

Declaration, by-laws and rules (pets, rentals, short-term stays) and the insurance policies.

03Red flags

  • Reserve fund below the study's planOften leads to fee hikes or a special assessment.
  • A special assessment, or one being discussedAsk who pays: you or the seller.
  • Ongoing lawsuitsCan affect fees, insurance and resale.
  • Large fee increase announcedBudget for it now.
  • Rules that block your plansRentals, pets or renovations you're counting on.
Ali's take

Give your lawyer the full certificate, not a summary, and give them time. A resale condo offer should always include a status certificate condition.
